newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran Asseman, Kyrgyzstan Airlines in new service.
newsitem.headline: Iran Asseman, Kyrgyzstan Airlines in new service.

text.p: State-owned Iran Asseman Airlines and Kyrgyzstan Airlines on Tuesday launched a joint weekly service between the countries' capitals, a spokesman for the Iranian airline said.

The once-weekly Bishkek-Tehran passenger service on Tuesdays will use a TU-154 or a TU-134, belonging to Kyrgyzstan Airlines, Asseman public relations manager Amirreza Mostafavi told Reuters by telephone from Tehran.
A cargo flight could be added later depending on demand, he added.
The launch follows the start last year of a weekly service between Bishkek and Mashhad, in northeastern Iran, and a weekly flight between Mashhad and Osh, in southern Kyrgyzstan, Mostafavi added.
Asseman also flies to Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, Turkmenistan, Tajikistan, and Dubai in the United Arab Emirates.
Asseman was formed by merging four private airlines after the 1979 Islamic revolution and is fully state-owned, Mostafavi said.
